question.text: If the function <math><mi>f</mi></math> defined on <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> by <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="" open="{" separators="|"><mrow><mtable><mtr><mtd><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></mtd><mtd><mtext>when </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi>k</mi></mtd><mtd><mo>,</mo><mtext>when </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mfenced></math>, is continuous, then <math><mi>k</mi></math> is equal to.

solution.text:
limx→0⁡fx=limx→0⁡ln⁡1+3xx-ln⁡1-2xx
=limx→0⁡3ln⁡1+3x3x+2ln1-2x-2x=3+2=5

limfx→0ln1+fxfx=1

∴fx, will be continuous if f0=limx→0⁡fx

Thus, k=5
